gbm_population_evidence.quote: Histopathologically proven diagnosis of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM, WHO grade 4) according to the 2021 WHO classification (including subtypes such as gliosarcoma).

candidate_evidence.quote: Azeliragon to be administered once daily for several days before, during, and after radiation therapy.

treatment_setting_evidence.quote: The study to be conducted is a phase 2 study in newly diagnosed "unmethylated" glioblastoma.

role_evidence.quote: this study will combine daily oral azeliragon with radiation treatment, followed by continued administration of azeliragon after completion of radiation therapy.

agents.drug_class_hint: RAGE (receptor for advanced glycation end products) antagonist, previously developed for Alzheimer's disease
agents.stated_antitumour_mechanism: may enhance the effectiveness of radiation, as well as have a delaying effect on disease progression

source_quote.quote: MGMT promoter methylation is negative based on local CLIA-certified commercial laboratory tests.
Histopathologically proven diagnosis of IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM, WHO grade 4) according to the 2021 WHO classification (including subtypes such as gliosarcoma).

coder_notes: Radiotherapy is not listed as an agent. Single-arm trial; unmethylated MGMT is an entry requirement but not linked to azeliragon mechanism, so not candidate-matched.
